bullets.title: MDB: CEO CJ Desai departs for Meta Enterprise Platform; Ittycheria returns as interim CEO
bullets.body: CJ Desai stepped down as MDB President & CEO effective immediately after <1 year to become Meta's Chief Enterprise Platform Officer, heading Meta's new enterprise AI business. Dev Ittycheria (CEO 2014–2025, scaled revenue $35M→$2.3B) returns as interim while a search firm hunts a permanent replacement; Q3/FY27 guidance reaffirmed ahead of tomorrow's Investor Day (11am–3:15pm ET at Nasdaq MarketSite). Street reaction varied: Wolfe maintains Outperform/$500 PT (21.8% upside) citing M&A floor at ~7x CY27 sales; DA Davidson maintains Buy; Hedgeye calls it a clear net negative, noting Desai was the face of go-to-market with large enterprise customers and the thesis rested on his ability to make Atlas relevant in enterprise AI; stock was down ~20% premarket.

bullets.title: META: Launches Enterprise Platform with Muse agent suite; poaches MDB CEO
bullets.body: Meta announced its Enterprise Platform as a new major business pillar, comprising the Muse agent, Meta Business Agent, Muse API, and Muse Code targeting businesses and developers. Muse is currently the #1 app in the Apple App Store; MSFT Copilot Super App exceeded 30M paid subs. Podcast analysis estimates META fair value at $650–750/share but sees less margin of safety at current levels, with some preferring GOOGL/AMZN at current prices given Meta's $130–145B AI capex this year and potentially ~$200B next year.

bullets.title: NVDA: $150B buyback increase to $235B total; UBS sees +$0.08 CY2027 EPS accretion
bullets.body: NVDA raised its share repurchase authorization by $150B to $235B total, to be executed by FYE2028, slightly above UBS's prior ~$200B model. UBS (Buy) estimates the incremental buyback adds ~$0.08 to CY2027 EPS vs. its $17.16 estimate. Separately, NVDA unveiled its Open Agent Safety Platform (OpenShell + Sentry) with partners including Anthropic, Microsoft, CrowdStrike, Cisco, ServiceNow, Salesforce, and Cloudflare; stock was up ~1.8% premarket.

bullets.title: MSFT: Copilot Super App relaunch with Home/Code/Autopilot; analysts see 10%+ M365 revenue growth upside
bullets.body: MSFT shares rose +3.7% after launching a unified Copilot AI OS with three tiers: Home (Chat/Cowork/Office), Code (custom solution building), and Autopilot (persistent proactive agent). Wells Fargo sees a doubling of Copilot seats plus 20% consumption uplift potentially adding 10+ percentage points to M365 Commercial Cloud revenue growth; RBC expects further details at MSFT Ignite in November. Current adoption remains low relative to the broader M365 base, presenting a large expansion runway.

bullets.title: RBLX: Jefferies downgrades to Underperform; Citi Buy but Week 39 CCUs down 17% YoY
bullets.body: Jefferies downgraded RBLX to Underperform, arguing recent gains overstate bookings growth given slower DAU expansion, algorithm headwinds, and elevated investment spend pressuring margins; stock was down ~5.4% premarket. Citi (Buy) notes Week 39 avg peak CCUs of 15.4M were down 3% sequentially and 17% YoY, though bookings track at $1.67B, just above company guidance of $1.65B; uncertainty remains whether moderation is seasonal or a structural signal.

bullets.title: MU: Citi raises PT ahead of earnings; tight DRAM supply, rising prices, HBM4 demand accelerating
bullets.body: Citi lifted MU's price target ahead of earnings on tight DRAM supply and rising spot prices (DDR5 up 6.4% M/M to $57.83; DDR5 RDIMM modules up 20.2% M/M to $2,163.50). Morgan Stanley's Joe Moore expects modest Q outperformance with November revenue at $57.56B vs. consensus $56.64B. Samsung is adding 4nm capacity for HBM4 demand; SK Hynix evaluating U.S. memory production; Citi hosting a post-earnings debrief with analyst Atif Malik on Sep 30 at 9:30pm EDT.

bullets.title: APP: eCommerce store count surges 11.7% w/w to 14,644 — fastest weekly growth on record
bullets.body: Citi (Buy) reports AppLovin's eCommerce store count hit 14,644 as of Sept 25, up 11.7% w/w, the fastest weekly growth since tracking began. 90% of the increase came from Hong Kong (+62.5% w/w) and China (+57.1% w/w), likely driven by AppLovin's Title Sponsor role at the ShopX eCommerce/AI summit Sept 17. AppLovin also acquired a new customer with a store rank of 2,339, the best since tracking began, suggesting higher-spend partnerships are forming.

bullets.title: DKNG: NFL Week 3 average for sportsbooks; handle growth decelerating sharply post-FIFA
bullets.body: NFL Week 3 saw favorites win ~60% of games (vs. 75%+ historical norm), implying normal hold dynamics for DKNG per UBS (Buy). However, Citi data shows DKNG's Q3 handle growth decelerated to +5% in August with GGR declining -20% y/y after July FIFA World Cup tailwinds; overall 3Q26 handle still +26% QTD and GGR +10%. Hedgeye has DKNG on its short bias list, citing September hold percentage weaker than expected.

bullets.title: LITE: Citi raises PT to $1,400 on OCS opportunity; nearest-term catalyst in optical sector
bullets.body: Citi raised LITE's price target to $1,400, based on a consistent 35x PE, with FY2027E and FY2028E EPS raised to $25 (from $23) and ~$41 (from $37) respectively; the OCS market is estimated at ~$11B. Morgan Stanley also flags LITE (alongside COHR) as having the nearest-term catalysts in optical — CPO/NPO announcements, InP supply chain strength, and yield improvements — with gross margin upside the bigger driver than demand.

bullets.title: Semis power/packaging bottleneck: chip-implied AI demand outpaces data center capacity by 3-4x through 2028
bullets.body: Jefferies warns AI data center deployments will reach 16–18 GW in 2026 and low-20s GW in 2027, but chip-implied demand is 34.5 GW (2027) and 54 GW (2028) — a 2.9x and 4.1x gap respectively. Advanced packaging is an immediate bottleneck (only 13 GW gross available), and energized land is the ultimate structural constraint. AMD EPYC processors are powering Meta Muse agent infrastructure; INTC CEO acknowledged the company can only satisfy ~50% of current CPU demand.

bullets.title: SNOW: Proposed $3.5B convertible note placement pressures stock -4.2% premarket
bullets.body: SNOW was down ~4.2% premarket on a proposed $3.5B convertible note placement, contributing to broader SaaS weakness. CRM was down -4.3%, HUBS -4.2%, NOW -3.6%, NET -2.7%, and ADBE -2.1% in premarket trading.

bullets.title: VZ: Citi Buy on improving 3Q setup; postpaid phone net adds tracking above consensus
bullets.body: Citi maintains Buy on VZ, expecting favorable 3Q results with improved postpaid phone net adds of ~220K vs. consensus 189K. The setup is seen as positive heading into earnings.

bullets.title: AAPL: Ordered to pay $5.7B in haptic patent damages; PeopleSoft security flaw hits ORCL
bullets.body: Apple was ordered to pay $5.7B in damages for haptic technology patent infringement brought by Taction Technology. Separately, Oracle's PeopleSoft enterprise software has a security flaw being actively exploited by the ShinyHunters hacker group. Both items are negative headline risks with limited long-term fundamental impact.

bullets.title: TLN, VST, OKLO, GEV: Oppenheimer expert call on SMR viability for data center power (9/30)
bullets.body: Oppenheimer is hosting an expert call on Sept 30 with Idaho National Lab CTO Brian Smith on whether SMRs can realistically meet surging data center power demand — covering deployment timelines, regulatory hurdles, and cost curves. Relevant for positioning in TLN, VST, OKLO, and GEV.

bullets.title: AMZN: Agentic shopping assistant reinforces product discovery control; positive AI infrastructure read-through
bullets.body: Amazon's agentic shopping assistant now covers the full discovery-to-checkout journey with long-term memory and preference tracking, retaining customer data inside AWS to prevent third-party disintermediation. Morgan Stanley and 22V highlight AMZN (alongside GOOGL) as better-positioned than META for agentic AI given entrenched cloud ecosystems; BKNG, EXPE, and ABNB are re-evaluating positioning as AI reshapes internet interaction.

bullets.title: UBS equity finance flows: AMD largest outflow since Oct 2025; NVDA most purchased; shorts up in RDDT, LITE
bullets.body: UBS weekly flows (week ended 9/25): AMD was the most sold stock on 9/22 with its largest outflow since Oct 2025; NVDA was the most purchased name as retail bought the dip in AI stocks. Top short interest increases: ADSK +41%, LITE +36%, RDDT +30%, PSKY +24%. Most covered WoW: SMCI, CRM, TSM, ORCL, SNOW, CSCO, AVGO. META saw profit-taking on 25 of last 27 days despite Muse download strength.

bullets.title: SHOP, CLS: Both pulled back ~2.6-2.7% on Canadian mid-morning; strong prior week gains
bullets.body: SHOP and CLS were both down ~2.6–2.7% in Canadian mid-morning trading on Sept 28, after strong prior-week performances (SHOP +12.2% w/w, CLS +11.1% w/w). SHOP is still down 9% YTD; CLS is up 27.3% YTD.

bullets.title: CVNA: Positioned as AI-era winner vs. franchise dealers; lower cost structure key advantage
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley flagged Carvana as best positioned for the AI/Muse era, with its lower cost structure providing flexibility as AI agents pressure retailers dependent on search friction. Traditional franchise dealers face greater disruption risk.

bullets.title: BofA's Hartnett: AI capex pushing hyperscalers to -$200B FCF; 5% 10yr yield is the ceiling
bullets.body: BofA CIO Hartnett warns hyperscalers (NVDA, MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN, AAPL) will spend $1–1.2T on AI capex next year, pushing free cash flow to negative $200B, making the AI trade "subservient" to bond market tolerance. The 'AI 10' now represents ~40% of S&P 500 market cap, matching 2000 tech bubble concentration. Hartnett prefers gold, commodities, small caps, and non-US equities; 5% on the 10-year is his informal ceiling.

bullets.title: NOK, CIEN: ECOC takeaways — Nokia aggressive on roadmap; CIEN targeting 50% gross margin pathway
bullets.body: From Morgan Stanley's ECOC follow-up: Nokia is running two DSP teams and has additional fab capacity coming online next year, with AI RAN gaining momentum across 19 customer trials. CIEN's $14B FY29 target excludes CPO/NPO/components upside; the 50% gross margin pathway is critical to the stock. Optical suppliers are sold out 12–18 months with gross margin upside the bigger driver of outperformance than demand growth.
